steps.title: Goal setting
steps.body: The process of identifying something you want to achieve and establishing measurable objectives and timeframes to work towards it. Goal setting provides direction, motivation and focus for performers.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Performance goals are generally more effective because they are within the performer's control. Even if you lose a match, you can still achieve a performance goal. This maintains motivation. Outcome goals are useful for long-term ambition but should be supported by performance goals.

steps.title: Goal Achievement Cycle
steps.body: Set goal → Work towards it → Evaluate progress → Adjust if needed → Achieve goal → Set new goal. This cycle ensures continuous improvement and prevents complacency after achieving a goal.

steps.title: PE Exam Tips — Goal Setting and SMART Targets
steps.body: 1. For Goal Setting and SMART Targets questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Goal Setting and SMART Targets to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between a performance goal and an outcome goal, using a sporting example. | What does each letter in SMART stand for? Explain why each element is important. | Rewrite this non-SMART goal as a SMART goal: "I want to be a better runner."

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always define SMART with full explanations - don't just list the words Use sporting examples for every concept - examiners want to see application Performance goals = within your control; Outcome goals = depend on others When writing SMART goals, include all five elements explicitly Remember that goals should be reviewed and adjusted regularly Link goal setting to motivation - this is the key benefit examiners look for
